newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Storehouse hopeful for Mothercare.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Storehouse hopeful for Mothercare.

text.p: British retail group Storehouse Plc, which said in November it hoped to reverse a decline in like-for-like sales at childrenswear chain Mothercare, on Friday predicted improvement by the end of the current business year.

"We said that by the year-end (March 31) we expected Mothercare to be on a better trend and there are signs that could still be true," Storehouse group chief executive Keith Edelman said in a telephone interview.

Storehouse said earlier on Friday that British sales at Mothercare were slightly higher in the six weeks to Christmas while overall sales were down by 0.8 percent and same-store sales dropped four percent.
But Edelman said trading since Christmas had improved, helped by Mothercare's new childrenswear range. He said the outlook for margins was favourable.

"We have improved margins at Mothercare and Bhs and managed in the first nine months to hold those margins. There is an opportunity for margin growth next year particularly in Childrens World when we convert them to Mothercare World," he said.
Storehouse, which bought Childrens World from Boots Plc, is converting the out-of-town sites into Mothercare World and eventually the Childrens World name will disappear.

At Childrens World, sales were down two percent in the six weeks to Christmas because of lower toy sales. Edelman said consumers appeared to be targeting electronic toys more closely at the expense of generic products.

"Toy sales were softer and probably it has something to do with the electronic area. Computers were very strong, even the very early computers," Edelman said, referring to the toy computers aimed at very young children.
"We will be reviewing our range, particularly at Childrens World and will have more electronic ranges next year," Edelman said.
